headline: NHAI and National Road Safety Board Deliberates on Strengthening Road Safety on National Highways
fullText:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways

NHAI and National Road Safety Board Deliberates on Strengthening Road Safety on National Highways

21 AUG 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi

In order to undertake a comprehensive review of road safety systems on the National Highway network, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and National Road Safety Board (NRSB) held an institutional meeting at NHAI Headquarters in New Delhi. The meeting was attended by Dr. Nitin R. Gokarn, Chairman, National Road Safety Board and NHAI Chairman, Shri Santosh Kumar Yadav. Other members of NRSB, officials from Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, NHAI, State Administrations, and Road safety experts were also present.

The meeting marked an important step towards establishing a structured institutional framework for sustained collaboration between NHAI and NRSB with the objective of strengthening road safety governance, enhancing National Highway safety standards and accelerating efforts towards reducing accidents on the National Highways.

During the meeting, NHAI presented a comprehensive view of the current status of road safety management on National Highways, covering road safety performance and emerging trends, institutional arrangements and governance, highway safety engineering and operations, road safety audits and black spot management, speed management, Intelligent Transport Systems and technology-enabled interventions.

The presentation also covered emergency response and post-crash care, monitoring and performance management systems, citizen engagement and user-centric services, commercial vehicle safety and driver welfare, besides identifying key challenges and future priorities for strengthening road safety across the National Highway network.

The discussions assessed the existing institutional arrangements, engineering practices and operational systems, while identifying opportunities to further strengthen road safety through the adoption of a Safe System approach. The approach encompasses six key strategic areas including Risk Identification, Safe Highway Engineering and Prevention; Safe Highway Operations, Commercial Vehicle Safety and Intelligent Transport Systems; Emergency Response, Incident Management and Citizen-Centric Safety; Digital Safety Management, Monitoring and Decision Support Systems; Performance Monitoring, Governance and Institutional Accountability and Strategic Roadmap for National Highway Road Safety. The two institutions will continue structured engagement through periodic review meetings to identify emerging challenges and strengthen road safety interventions.

The deliberations also included a detailed diagnostic review of the existing road safety ecosystem on National Highways, with emphasis on technology-enabled interventions and emergency response mechanisms. Dr. Nitin R. Gokarn, Chairman, NRSB, appreciated NHAI’s adoption of advanced technology tools for enhancing road safety, including the deployment of Advanced Traffic Management Systems (ATMS), predictive Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions and digital mapping of ambulances to strengthen incident response and emergency services. He further emphasized the need for identifying top 10 accident-prone locations across the country, along with strengthening first-response capabilities at toll plazas by providing first-aid training to toll plaza personnel, enabling them to provide timely assistance to road accident victims. It was also emphasized that NHAI field offices should work closely with state administrations and keep them informed about the road safety initiatives for better coordination.

The interaction between NRSB and NHAI marks the beginning of a structured and sustained institutional partnership focused on strengthening the road safety ecosystem on National Highways.

headline: Sarbananda Sonowal Inaugurates ₹427.80 Crore Projects at Paradip Port, Marks 18.5-Metre Deep-Draft Capability
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

Sarbananda Sonowal Inaugurates ₹427.80 Crore Projects at Paradip Port, Marks 18.5-Metre Deep-Draft Capability

Sonowal Witnesses ₹1,580.36-Crore Concession Agreements for 100% Berth Mechanisation by 2030

Sonowal planted one-millionth tree as Paradip expands capacity and green cover

PPA Backs Job-Linked Skilling for Youth, Sustainable Fishing Practices for Coastal Communities

Under PM Narendra Modi, India’s Maritime Sector Has Become an Anchor of Viksit & Atmanirbhar Bharat by 2047: Sarbananda Sonowal

21 AUG 2026 5:42PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal inaugurated seven major infrastructure projects worth ₹427.80 crore at Paradip Port Authority (PPA) in Paradip, Odisha, marking the port's 18.5-metre deep-draft capability and its one-millionth tree milestone, while also witnessing the signing of concession agreements for three mechanisation projects worth ₹1,580.36 crore aimed at further strengthening Paradip's capacity, efficiency and cargo-handling capabilities.

The projects span navigation, connectivity, safety, sustainability, residential infrastructure and community development, while the mechanisation projects are aimed at improving cargo handling and reducing vessel turnaround time.

The Union Minister was joined by Odisha Minister of State (Independent Charge), Department of Industries, Skill Development and Technical Education, Sampad Chandra Swain; Jagatsinghpur MP Bibhu Prasad Tarai; Paradip Port Authority Chairman P. L. Haranadh, IRTS; Deputy Chairman T. Venu Gopal; senior officials, stakeholders and members of the Paradip Port community.

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said the investments would strengthen Paradip's position as a major maritime gateway and create wider economic opportunities across the eastern region.

“The expansion of Paradip Port's capacity is not only about strengthening one port; it is about creating a growth multiplier for eastern India. With deeper drafts, modern cargo-handling infrastructure, improved connectivity and greater mechanisation, Paradip is well positioned to drive trade, logistics, industry and employment across the region and contribute to India's emergence as a globally competitive maritime economy,” Sarbananda Sonowal said.

SEVEN PROJECTS WORTH ₹427.80 CRORE

The ₹427.80 crore project package includes:

18.5-metre deep-draft capability: ₹352 crore: Capital dredging will enable Paradip Port to handle fully laden Capesize vessels in its inner harbour, improving economies of scale and helping reduce vessel turnaround and logistics costs.

Atharbanki Second New Bridge: ₹24.89 crore: The 500-metre, three-lane bridge, with footpaths and a dedicated pipeline corridor across Atharbanki Creek, is expected to ease congestion along a route used by nearly 3,000 trucks daily.

Sports Hostel: ₹2.10 crore: The facility will provide accommodation and amenities for aspiring athletes, supporting youth development.

Administrative Office Building façade upgrade: ₹12.18 crore: The redevelopment of the 1980s-era building and its surroundings, executed by NBCC (India) Ltd., includes improved parking and circulation facilities.

Piped Natural Gas supply to residential quarters: ₹20 crore: Developed in partnership with Bharat Petroleum Corp. Ltd., the first phase will extend PNG connectivity to 546 residential quarters in Madhuban. The facility is expected to reduce household gas expenses by up to 40% and make Paradip the first major port to provide PNG to its residential township.

Advanced Vessel Traffic Management and Information System: ₹15.50 crore: Developed with the National Technology Centre for Ports, Waterways and Coasts at IIT Madras, the system integrates solid-state radar, artificial intelligence, AIS, CCTV, oil-spill monitoring and 3D visualisation to monitor vessel movement up to 20 nautical miles from a modern ATC-style signal station.

One-millionth tree: Sonowal planted Paradip Port's one-millionth tree, marking a milestone in the port's plantation and green-cover initiatives.

The green milestone builds on plantation drives initiated after the 1999 Super Cyclone, with the Authority intensifying plantation activities over the past four years. PPA said nearly one lakh trees have been planted annually during this period, with employees, stakeholders and local communities contributing to the effort. The port said the initiative is aimed at expanding green cover, supporting biodiversity and strengthening environmental sustainability.

₹1,580.36 CRORE MECHANISATION PROJECTS

PPA also signed concession agreements for three projects, with an investment of ₹1,580.36 crore, as part of its plan to achieve 100% berth mechanisation by 2030, compared with the current level of 80%. They will support faster, safer and cleaner cargo handling while reducing vessel turnaround times and logistics costs.

The agreements cover the 5 MTPA South Quay mechanisation project, awarded to M/s Yogayatan Paradip SQB Terminal Pvt. Ltd. at an estimated investment of ₹498.69 crore on a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) basis; the 8 MTPA Multipurpose Berth mechanisation project, awarded to M/s Kalinga Bulk Terminal Paradip Pvt. Ltd. at ₹630.67 crore, also on a BOT basis; and the 10 MTPA captive CQ-III mechanisation project, awarded to M/s AMNS Paradip Logistics Pvt. Ltd. at an estimated ₹451 crore.

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said the development of Paradip is part of the wider transformation underway in India's maritime sector. “Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India has embarked on an unprecedented phase of maritime modernisation. Over the past 12 years, we have fundamentally strengthened our ports, waterways, shipping and maritime capabilities, making the sector a powerful engine of growth and the anchor of an Atmanirbhar Bharat and our journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047,” Sonowal said.

PPA also highlighted the outcomes of two CSR-funded skill-development initiatives undertaken during 2025-26. The Authority provided financial assistance to the Centre of Excellence in Maritime and Shipbuilding (CEMS), Visakhapatnam, under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, for placement-linked training of 168 unemployed youth from Odisha in Bhubaneswar. Training covered roles including inventory clerk, courier associate operations and supply chain executive, with the trained candidates subsequently placed across various companies.

PPA also supported the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry in conducting skill-development programmes for Odisha's fishing communities, particularly around Paradip Fishing Harbour. The programmes covered fish quality and hygienic handling, responsible fishing practices, distribution of square-mesh cod-ends and bio-toilets, and awareness on turtle excluder devices and sustainable fisheries.

The initiatives are aimed at improving hygiene and safety in fishing operations while supporting sustainable fisheries and alternative livelihood opportunities for fishing communities.

headline: Government Strengthens Scholarship Delivery through Direct Benefit Transfer for SC and OBC Students
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Strengthens Scholarship Delivery through Direct Benefit Transfer for SC and OBC Students

₹30.81 Crore Released under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes in East Godavari District during 2025–26

21 AUG 2026 5:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Government continues to strengthen educational support for students belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) through Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes. Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) has made the disbursal process simpler, faster and more transparent by transferring scholarship assistance directly into the Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of eligible beneficiaries.

During 2025–26, ₹30.81 crore was released to SC and OBC students under these scholarship schemes in East Godavari district. This included ₹20.80 crore under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students and ₹2.38 crore under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs and Others. Additionally, ₹6.83 crore was released under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC students and ₹0.80 crore under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC students.

Available beneficiary data for 2025–26 indicates that 44,746 students received assistance under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs, while 32,813 students were covered under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs and Others. The corresponding figures under the Post-Matric and Pre-Matric Scholarship Schemes for OBC students were 13,658 and 1,997, respectively.

Constituency-wise data for the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs and the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs and Others is not maintained on the National Scholarship Portal. Therefore, the figures of 44,746 and 32,813 represent combined data for East Godavari, Eluru and Kakinada districts, as provided by the National Scholarship Portal–National Informatics Centre.

Applications under the scholarship schemes are invited through designated online portals operated by States and Union Territories. The release of the Central share is contingent upon the disbursal of the State or Union Territory share and the submission of finally verified beneficiary data to the National Scholarship Portal.

States and Union Territories, as implementing agencies, determine the modalities for inviting, processing and verifying applications, integrating relevant databases and managing other aspects of implementation. The DBT mechanism has strengthened accurate targeting, improved efficiency and ensured that financial assistance reaches eligible students directly.

Issues concerning the implementation of scholarship schemes, including delays in processing renewal applications, are regularly taken up with States, Union Territories and other stakeholders for timely resolution. The schemes are also monitored through national-level Chintan Shivirs, regional meetings and national conferences involving officials and concerned stakeholders.

headline: Government Acts to Curb Sugar Price Rise, Ensure Adequate Availability During Festive Season
fullText:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

Government Acts to Curb Sugar Price Rise, Ensure Adequate Availability During Festive Season

21 AUG 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi

Sugar prices have increased in recent weeks, from ₹48.18 per kg on 20 July 2026 to ₹55.70 per kg on 20 August 2026. The Government is closely monitoring the situation and has taken a series of measures to ensure adequate availability of sugar and stable prices for consumers.

Rise in sugar prices cannot be attributed to ethanol

It is incorrect to attribute the recent increase in sugar prices to diversion of sugar for ethanol production.

In fact, the share of sugar diverted for ethanol has declined from around 12% in 2022-23 to around 9% in 2025-26. Moreover, nearly three-fourths of the ethanol produced in the country now comes from grains, particularly maize.

The present increase in sugar prices is due to a combination of factors, including lower-than-expected domestic production, increased demand ahead of the festive season, weather-related damage to the sugarcane crop, tightening global sugar supplies and speculation and hoarding by some sections of the industry.

Sugar production lower than initial estimates

Sugar production during the current season is expected to be around 306 LMT, compared to the initial estimate of around 343 LMT by sugarcane-growing States.

Production has been affected by Red Rot and Top Borer disease in sugarcane, as well as waterlogging caused by excess rainfall.

Despite the lower than estimated production, adequate sugar stocks are available in the country to meet domestic demand until the new crushing season begins in October.

Sugar prices are rising globally too

The tightening of sugar supplies is a global phenomenon and is not limited to India.

The global sugar deficit for 2026-27 is estimated at around 33 LMT. Concerns over weather conditions have further affected the global outlook.

As a result, international sugar prices have risen sharply from $474 per tonne on 30 June 2026 to $552 per tonne on 20 August 2026 — an increase of over 16% in less than two months.

Ethanol programme has helped farmers and strengthened sugar mills

India normally produces around 320-340 LMT of sugar annually, against domestic consumption of around 280-290 LMT. In years of surplus production, excess stocks block the funds of sugar mills and can delay payments to sugarcane farmers.

Diversion of excess sugar towards ethanol has helped address this structural problem and improved the financial health of sugar mills.

The results are visible. As on 20 August 2026, 97% of sugarcane dues for the 2025-26 sugar season have already been paid to farmers.

The improved financial position of sugar mills has also reduced their dependence on Government support. While around ₹14,600 crore of subsidy was provided to the sugar industry between 2014 and 2021, no such subsidy has been announced since 2021-22.

At the same time, sugar prices for consumers have remained broadly stable over the longer term, increasing by only around 3% annually between August 2024 and July 2026.

Government acting against hoarding and to increase supply

The Government has observed that speculation and hoarding by some sugar mills and traders have also contributed to the recent price increase. Several steps have therefore been taken:

A stock limit of 400 tonnes has been imposed on sugar dealers across the country from 1 August to 30 November 2026.

From 1 September, bulk consumers will not be permitted to hold sugar stocks exceeding 15 days of consumption.

Joint teams of Central and State Government officials are carrying out physical verification of sugar stocks at mills to check hoarding and artificial scarcity.

As a precautionary measure, the Government has decided to permit duty-free import of 10 LMT of raw sugar to further augment domestic availability.

States and sugar mills have been advised to begin crushing from 15 October 2026. This is expected to raise October sugar production from the usual 3-4 LMT to more than 10 LMT, further improving availability during the festive season.

The Government remains committed to protecting the interests of both consumers and sugarcane farmers. It will continue to closely monitor sugar stocks, prices and market practices and take all necessary measures to prevent hoarding and unwarranted price increases while ensuring timely payment of dues to farmers.

headline: From Financial Hardship to Academic Excellence: How the Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship Supported Dr. Paramananda Naik's Journey in Anthropology
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Financial Hardship to Academic Excellence: How the Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship Supported Dr. Paramananda Naik's Journey in Anthropology

21 AUG 2026 5:26PM by PIB Delhi

For students from socially and economically marginalized communities, limited financial resources and restricted academic exposure can create significant barriers to pursuing advanced education and research. Timely fellowship support can enable aspiring scholars to continue their studies, undertake meaningful research and build careers in higher education.

Demonstrating the transformative role of educational assistance, Dr. Paramananda Naik, a 35-year-old scholar belonging to the Scheduled Caste (PANO) community, overcame financial and social barriers to complete his Ph.D. in Anthropology and become an Assistant Professor in the Department of Anthropology at Utkal University, Bhubaneswar.

Coming from a socially and economically marginalized background, Dr. Naik faced considerable financial hardship while pursuing higher education. Limited economic resources made it difficult for him to meet expenses related to books, accommodation, field visits, research activities and other requirements of his doctoral studies.

As a second-generation learner from his community, he also encountered social and educational barriers, including limited academic exposure and restricted access to quality higher education and research opportunities. Despite these challenges, he remained determined to pursue advanced studies and establish himself as a teacher and researcher in Anthropology.

With strong family support and personal determination, Dr. Naik continued his academic journey with the aspiration of contributing to society through teaching, research and the study of Anthropology.

A turning point came when Dr. Naik received assistance under the Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students. Under the UGC-RGNF-SC, he received financial support of ₹16,000 per month from 2016 to 2019.

The fellowship provided crucial assistance for his academic expenses, fieldwork, research activities and overall educational development. By reducing financial stress, it enabled him to focus fully on his doctoral research and higher studies.

With the support of the fellowship, Dr. Naik successfully completed his Ph.D. in Anthropology. His academic journey subsequently led him to secure a regular position as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Anthropology at Utkal University, Bhubaneswar.

Today, he is actively engaged in teaching, research and mentoring students while contributing to academic and social development. His professional progress has brought significant economic stability and strengthened his ability to support his family.

The fellowship played an important role in Dr. Naik's educational, professional and socio-economic advancement. It not only supported the completion of his doctoral research but also created a strong foundation for his career in higher education.

According to Dr. Naik, 'The fellowship reduced my financial stress and enabled me to focus fully on my research and higher studies. It helped me complete my Ph.D. and build a career as a teacher and researcher in Anthropology.'

Dr. Paramananda Naik's journey highlights how timely financial assistance can help students from marginalized communities overcome structural barriers and fulfil their academic aspirations. From facing financial hardship during higher education to serving as an Assistant Professor, his story reflects determination, the value of family support and the empowering role of educational fellowships in creating pathways to academic and professional success.

headline: From Sanitation Helper to Mechanised Sanitation Entrepreneur: How NAMASTE-SUY Helped Neeraj Build a Safer and Self-Reliant Livelihood
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Sanitation Helper to Mechanised Sanitation Entrepreneur: How NAMASTE-SUY Helped Neeraj Build a Safer and Self-Reliant Livelihood

21 AUG 2026 5:23PM by PIB Delhi

For sanitation workers seeking safer and more sustainable livelihoods, limited access to finance and mechanised equipment can be a major barrier. Timely financial assistance can help them move away from hazardous manual practices, establish independent enterprises and secure dignity at work.

Demonstrating the transformative potential of mechanisation, Neeraj, a 40-year-old resident of Bhikanpur village in Muradnagar, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, established his own mechanised sanitation service enterprise with support under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) component of the NAMASTE Scheme.

Neeraj belongs to the Scheduled Caste (Jatav) community and comes from a financially disadvantaged family. He began working at a young age to support his household and gradually entered sanitation-related work. For several years, he worked as a helper in sewer and septic-tank cleaning operations alongside local sanitation workers and private contractors.

Although continuous hard work gave him valuable experience, the work remained physically demanding, unsafe and poorly paid. He often worked long hours with limited safety arrangements and depended on contractors for irregular employment opportunities.

As the sole earning member of a family comprising his wife and two children, Neeraj faced constant pressure in meeting household expenses, educational costs and healthcare needs. His monthly income of approximately ₹8,000 was insufficient and irregular. He often struggled to pay his son's school fees on time and could not always arrange proper medical treatment for his daughter during illness.

Along with economic hardship, Neeraj faced occupational risks, social stigma and discrimination associated with sanitation work. Limited educational and technical exposure, lack of savings and difficulty in arranging capital prevented him from purchasing modern sanitation machinery and establishing an independent enterprise.

Neeraj aspired to establish his own mechanised sanitation service so that he could work independently, safely and with dignity. He wanted to reduce his dependence on contractors, expand sanitation services in Muradnagar and nearby areas, and provide better education, healthcare and opportunities for his children.

A turning point came in 2023 when Neeraj received financial assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana component of the NAMASTE Scheme. The support enabled him to purchase three tractors fitted with suction machines and establish a mechanised sanitation service enterprise.

The total project cost was 11,90,400, comprising a loan amount of ₹7,67,800 and an upfront capital subsidy of 4,22,600. This assistance gave Neeraj access to the vehicles and suction equipment required to undertake sewer and septic-tank cleaning operations independently.

The mechanised equipment significantly improved the safety, efficiency and dignity of his work while reducing dependence on hazardous manual sanitation practices. Instead of working under private contractors, Neeraj now independently manages sanitation operations in Muradnagar and nearby areas of Ghaziabad.

Before receiving assistance, Neeraj earned approximately 8,000 per month as a sanitation helper. After establishing his mechanised enterprise, his monthly income increased to approximately ₹30,000-40,000. Even after paying a monthly EMI of ₹17,149 and meeting operational expenses, he is able to maintain a stable income and support his family more comfortably.

The increase in income has strengthened the family's financial position. Neeraj can now pay his children's educational expenses on time, provide better healthcare and manage household requirements with reduced financial stress. The intervention has also enhanced his confidence, social recognition and dignity as an independent sanitation entrepreneur.

Neeraj's family, which supported and encouraged him through years of hardship, now looks towards the future with renewed hope. He plans to expand his mechanised sanitation services across nearby areas and build a stable and sustainable livelihood for his family.

Neeraj's journey demonstrates how mechanisation and targeted financial assistance can help sanitation workers overcome economic and occupational barriers. His progress stands as an encouraging example of how the NAMASTE-Swachhta Udyami Yojana promotes safety, dignity, self-employment and financial independence.

headline: 29 FDI Investments Worth ₹4,895.65 Crore Reported Under Revised Framework
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

29 FDI Investments Worth ₹4,895.65 Crore Reported Under Revised Framework

Revised FDI Framework Facilitates Investment with Non-Controlling Beneficial Ownership from Land Bordering Countries

21 AUG 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi

A total of 29 FDI investments have been reported under the revised framework up to 20 August 2026, involving proposed FDI of ₹4,895.65 crore. These investments span a range of sectors, including Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Information & Communication, Manufacturing, Pharmaceuticals, Data Centres and Transport Services, among others.

The 29 investments have been reported by investors/entities based in jurisdictions including Mauritius, the United States, the Republic of Korea, Japan, Singapore, Luxembourg and the Cayman Islands.

The revised framework facilitates and expedites the flow of foreign investment into India by removing the requirement of prior Government approval in cases involving non-controlling Land Bordering Countries (LBC) ownership of up to 10%. The reform provides greater certainty to investors, reduces transaction time and further strengthens the ease of doing business in India.

With Press Note 2 of 2026 and the consequent amendment to the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019, notified on 1 May 2026, the beneficial ownership test is now applied at the level of the investor entity. Investors with non-controlling LBC ownership of up to 10% can invest through the automatic route, subject to applicable sectoral caps, entry routes and other conditions. The investor entity can proceed with the investment without obtaining any other approval, after reporting the relevant information to the Government.

Earlier, foreign investors with beneficial ownership from LBCs of India were required to obtain prior Government approval under Press Note 3 of 2020, even where such LBC ownership was very small. This had been a long-standing concern among investors seeking greater clarity and ease of investment.

fullText:

Office of Pr. CCA, Delhi celebrates National Senior Citizens Day; Super Senior pensioners felicitated

21 AUG 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Office of the Principal Controller of Communication Accounts (Pr. CCA), Delhi, under the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, celebrated National Senior Citizens Day today at Sanchar Lekha Bhawan, Prasad Nagar, New Delhi. The programme, organised for the pensioners of the Department, was chaired by Ms. Vandana Gupta, Controller General of Communication Accounts (CGCA). The celebration was held to acknowledge and honour the valuable contribution and the services rendered to the nation by the senior and super senior pensioners of the Department of Telecommunications.

The felicitation ceremony formed the centrepiece of the celebration. Senior pensioners, including several who have crossed ninety years of age, were honoured for their long and dedicated service to the Department and to the nation. The eldest pensioner felicitated on the occasion was shri Parshuram Sharma aged 99 years, who superannuated from the Department of Telecommunication (DoT) in 1987. The felicitation of the nonagenarian pensioners was warmly received by the gathering.

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Vandana Gupta, CGCA, emphasized that our senior pensioners are the living memory of this Department. Our responsibility towards them did not end on the day they superannuated; it merely changed form. Ensuring that their pension reaches them on time, and that they are heard, respected and cared for, is not a courtesy this office extends — it is a duty this office owes.

A health check-up camp was also organised during the programme, at which the senior citizens and pensioners present availed themselves of basic health check-up, Pulmonary Function Test (PFT) and eye check-up facilities, conducted on the spot by a team of qualified medical professionals. The participants were examined and counselled on their findings and were advised on preventive care and the importance of periodic health monitoring in advanced age. The initiative was warmly appreciated by the elderly pensioners, for whom the availability of such services at the venue itself proved a considerable convenience.

The programme further featured awareness sessions on cyber security and financial safety for senior citizens. As elderly citizens are often vulnerable to online frauds, phishing attempts and financial scams, the sessions underlined the importance of safe digital practices and of vigilance while using online services. Experts shared practical guidance on protecting personal information, identifying fraudulent activity and ensuring secure financial transactions. Organised in collaboration with the State Bank of India (SBI), the initiative sought to enhance digital and financial awareness among senior citizens and to enable them to access digital services with confidence while safeguarding themselves against emerging cyber and financial threats.

An informative lecture was thereafter delivered by Dr. Babita Yadav , Senior Research Officer of the Ministry of AYUSH, who underscored the significance of healthy living, preventive healthcare and India's traditional systems of wellness in sustaining an active and independent lifestyle in advanced age. The pensioners were apprised of simple and sustainable practices including Yoga, balanced dietary habits and the Ayurvedic principles of Dinacharya (daily regimen) that may be readily adopted to enhance physical and mental well-being in the later years of life.

A Know Your Pension (KYP) and Digital Life Certificate (DLC) camp was also organised on the sidelines of the event. Pensioners were assisted at the KYP counter in accessing and understanding their records on the SAMPANN portal. At the DLC counter, life certificates were submitted on the spot through Jeevan Pramaan using face authentication.

The programme provided a meaningful platform for interaction between the senior pensioners and the officers of the Department, and reflected the Department's sustained commitment to the welfare, dignity and well-being of its senior citizens.

headline: DARPG organises 20th National e-Governance Webinar on Government Process Re-engineering for Digital Transformation
fullText:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

DARPG organises 20th National e-Governance Webinar on Government Process Re-engineering for Digital Transformation

AgriStack and e-Jagriti, National Award-winning initiatives, showcase technology-enabled transformation in agricultural governance and consumer dispute resolution

21 AUG 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) organised the 20th National e-Governance Webinar (NeGW) under the theme “Government Process Re-engineering by use of technology for Digital Transformation (Central Level)”. The webinar was chaired by Shri Avanish Kumar Mishra, Joint Secretary, DARPG.

The webinar showcased two National Award-winning initiatives recognised under the Central Level Initiatives category of the National Awards for e-Governance 2026 — AgriStack of the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and e-Jagriti of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs. The initiatives demonstrated how technology-enabled process re-engineering can improve efficiency, transparency, accessibility and citizen-centric service delivery.

The following award-winning initiatives were presented:

AgriStack: Dr. Pramod Kumar Meherda, Additional Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, presented the Gold Award-winning AgriStack initiative. AgriStack is a Digital Public Infrastructure initiative aimed at modernising agricultural governance and service delivery across the country.

AgriStack is built around three core registries — the Farmers’ Registry, Crop Sown Registry and Geo-referenced Village Maps — providing a digital foundation for verified farmer identification, land holdings and crops sown. The initiative follows a federated architecture, with the registries created, owned and managed by States and Union Territories while ensuring interoperability across the national agricultural ecosystem.

The Digital Crop Survey is operational across 31.36 crore plots in 648 districts, while more than 10 crore unique Farmer IDs have been created and 5.52 lakh geo-referenced village maps have been completed. Farmer IDs are also being integrated with major programmes including PMFBY, PM Asha, MahaDBT and MSP Procurement.

AgriStack demonstrates how technology-driven process re-engineering can strengthen transparency, enable verified delivery of government schemes and reduce dependence on fragmented and manual processes.

e-Jagriti: Shri G. Mayil Muthu Kumaran, Deputy Director General, National Informatics Centre, presented the Silver Award-winning e-Jagriti initiative, which demonstrates how digital platforms can transform consumer dispute resolution.

e-Jagriti establishes a unified national digital ecosystem for consumer dispute resolution across the National, State and District Consumer Commissions. The platform replaces fragmented legacy systems with a standardised, end-to-end digital workflow covering online filing, digital scrutiny, payment processing, hearings, orders and disposal of cases.

The platform also integrates virtual and hybrid hearings, automated cause lists, real-time notifications, analytics dashboards and mobile application support, enabling consumers and other stakeholders to access and manage consumer dispute resolution processes digitally.

The initiative has transformed traditionally paper-based and time-consuming processes into a seamless digital experience, reducing physical visits and manual dependency while improving transparency, accessibility and efficiency in consumer dispute redressal.

The webinar witnessed participation from senior officials across approximately, 1200+ Officials, including Central Ministries, State Governments, District and Local Bodies, administrations from across the country and officials of DARPG.

At the conclusion of the webinar, Shri Hari K Bhatt, Deputy Secretary, DARPG, delivered the Vote of Thanks. He thanked the speakers and participants and encouraged States, Districts, Local Bodies and Central Ministries to examine the showcased initiatives for adoption and replication in their respective areas of governance.

The webinar reaffirmed the importance of technology-enabled Government Process Re-engineering in transforming public service delivery and strengthening efficient, transparent, accessible and citizen-centric governance.

headline: Ken-Betwa Link Project
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

Ken-Betwa Link Project

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

21 AUG 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi

About the Project

What is the Ken-Betwa Link Project?

The Ken–Betwa Link Project (KBLP) is a major water-resources development project intended to address the long-standing water scarcity and irrigation challenges of the Bundelkhand region of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

The project envisages transfer of water from the Ken basin to the Betwa basin through a system comprising the Daudhan Dam, link canal and associated works. KBLP is the first priority project under the National Perspective Plan for Interlinking of Rivers to enter the implementation stage.

What is the scheme of the project?

This project involves transfer of water from the Ken to the Betwa River through construction of the 96.7 m high Daudhan Dam on the Ken River in Panna and Chhatarpur districts of Madhya Pradesh, about 40 km from Khajuraho. A 216.465 km-long Ken–Betwa Link Canal will take off near the Daudhan Dam and merge into Barua Sagar near Jhansi. Other components include the Lower Orr Project, Kotha Barrage, and Bina Complex Multipurpose Project.

The Project also includes various irrigation and water infrastructure works to be implemented by the Governments of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, including modernization and strengthening of existing canal systems, renovation of tanks and weirs, construction of barrages, development of pumping and pressurized pipe/micro-irrigation systems, stabilization and development of new command areas, and implementation of associated water supply and irrigation projects.

What is the total cost of the project

The total cost of the project is ₹44,605 crore.

What is the status of this project

The foundation stone of the project was laid by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 25th December 2024. The dam is under construction, while work on the canal is yet to begin. The Lower Orr Project, Kotha Barrage, and Bina Complex Multipurpose Project are under construction. Preparation of DPR of other state-specific projects of MP and UP is also under finalisation stage. The Project is scheduled for completion in 2030.

Why is this project needed?

Bundelkhand region has historically faced recurrent water scarcity, dependence on rainfall, inadequate irrigation facilities, declining groundwater availability in several areas and vulnerability of agriculture to drought.

The Ken Betwa Link Project is designed to provide more dependable water availability for irrigation and drinking-water requirements while also generating renewable energy and supporting broader regional development. The project is therefore not merely an irrigation project; it is envisaged as a comprehensive water-security and regional-development initiative for Bundelkhand.

What are the main benefits of the project?

The Project will provide irrigation to 10.62 lakh ha, drinking water to about 62 lakh people, and generate 103 MW of hydropower and 27 MW of solar power. Thus, it will supply clean drinking water, electricity, and reliable year-round irrigation across vast farmlands in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, permanently resolving the long-standing water crisis in the Bundelkhand region.

Which areas will benefit from this project?

The project will benefit the water-starved Bundelkhand region across Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, covering districts such as Chhatarpur, Newari, Tikamgarh, Panna, Sagar, Damoh, Datia, Vidisha, Shivpuri, and Raisen in M.P., and Banda, Mahoba, Jhansi and Lalitpur in U.P.

Will the Ken–Betwa Link Project create new jobs in the local area?

Yes. The Ken–Betwa Link Project (KBLP) is generating employment opportunities in the local area, particularly during the ongoing construction phase. Employment is being generated in civil construction, engineering, transportation, material supply, equipment operation, security, services and other ancillary activities. Local shops, transporters, suppliers and service providers are also benefiting from increased economic activity. In the long term, improved irrigation and water availability will support agriculture and allied activities, creating further livelihood and employment opportunities in the region.

How will the Ken–Betwa Link Project improve agriculture in Bundelkhand?

The Ken–Betwa Link Project is providing more reliable irrigation water, reducing dependence on uncertain rainfall and helping farmers plan agricultural activities with greater confidence. The improved availability of irrigation water is expected to support increased cropping intensity, higher crop productivity, crop diversification, cultivation of high-value crops, reduced vulnerability to drought and improved farm incomes, thereby strengthening rural livelihoods in the Bundelkhand region.

Will KBLP eliminate drought in Bundelkhand?

It would not be appropriate to claim that the project will completely eliminate drought.

Rather, KBLP is intended to substantially improve water security and drought resilience in its command and beneficiary areas by providing dependable irrigation and drinking-water support.

Will groundwater levels improve?

The availability of surface water for irrigation and other uses can reduce excessive dependence on groundwater in appropriate areas. The project also envisages rejuvenation/feeding of tanks along the link canal, wherever technically feasible, which can contribute to groundwater recharge and local water security.

Actual groundwater improvement will depend on local hydrogeological conditions and sustainable groundwater-use practices.

How does the wider region gain from this development?

By protecting crops from drought, it will boost harvests, reduce losses, and raise family incomes for farmers, while better utilities and transport links create new jobs and uplift everyday living standards for the entire community. It is expected to boost socio-economic prosperity in this backward region through increased agricultural activities, employment generation, and reduced distress migration. Better infrastructure attracts new schools, healthcare clinics, commercial markets, and agro-industries, transforming the area into a prosperous one.

Will downstream villages face any water shortage?

No. Continuous minimum environmental water release is strictly maintained around the year to ensure that downstream farming, drinking water needs, and aquatic ecosystems remain undisturbed. Similarly, the water infrastructure created under the region would also enhance the groundwater in the region.

How are flood risks managed during heavy monsoons?

The dam will act as a cushion against floods. Its automated spillway gates and 24/7 control rooms monitor water inflow to prevent sudden flooding in low-lying villages.

Are the benefits of KBLP greater than its impacts?

The project has been evaluated through the prescribed technical, economic, environmental and social assessment processes. KBLP is intended to deliver large-scale benefits in irrigation, drinking water and renewable energy while implementing mitigation and R&R measures for unavoidable impacts.

The appropriate approach is therefore not to ignore the impacts, but to minimize, mitigate, compensate and responsibly manage them while delivering the intended public benefits.

Is the Ken–Betwa Link Project beneficial only to farmers?

No. The Ken–Betwa Link Project (KBLP) provides benefits beyond irrigation to farmers. It supports farmers through irrigation facilities; rural and urban populations through drinking water supply; the energy sector through hydropower generation; and local communities through employment, infrastructure and increased economic activity. Overall, the project is strengthening water security, agricultural development and socio-economic growth in the Bundelkhand region.

Will KBLP improve transportation infrastructure?

Major water infrastructure projects require construction and improvement of access roads, bridges, approaches and other associated infrastructure. Where such infrastructure is developed or upgraded as part of the project, it will facilitate improved connectivity to nearby areas.

Will project roads benefit local communities?

Project-related roads and connectivity infrastructure will facilitate secondary benefits to surrounding communities and people at large such as:

movement of agricultural produce;

access to markets;

access to schools and healthcare;

construction and economic activities;

movement of people and goods; and

access to project facilities.

Will KBLP directly develop a new transport corridor?

KBLP is primarily a water-resource and energy project. Any transport-related benefit should therefore be described in terms of project-associated roads, bridges and improved connectivity, rather than presenting KBLP as a dedicated transport project unless a particular transport facility has been formally approved as part of the project.

Why is drinking-water supply an important component of the Ken–Betwa Link Project (KBLP)?

Drinking-water supply is an important component of KBLP because water security is essential not only for agriculture but also for the well-being of rural and urban communities. Reliable drinking water helps improve public health, sanitation and household security, reduces the time spent by families, particularly women, in collecting water, and supports education, livelihoods and overall quality of life. Thus, KBLP has both agricultural and human-development benefits.

Land, Villages and People Affected

Why is land required for the Ken–Betwa Link Project (KBLP)?

Land is required for construction and development of various permanent and temporary project components of KBLP, including the Daudhan Dam and its appurtenant structures, reservoir/submergence area, Ken–Betwa Link Canal, powerhouses, access roads, project infrastructure, colonies, construction facilities and other ancillary works required for implementation of the project.

How many villages are affected by the project in Madhya Pradesh?

22 villages are affected — 8 in Panna district and 14 in Chhatarpur district.

Whether a public hearing was conducted for the Ken–Betwa Link Project?

Yes. Public hearings were conducted as part of the Environmental Clearance process for the Ken–Betwa Link Project, in accordance with the provisions of the EIA Notification, 2006. The concerns and suggestions raised by the local people and other stakeholders during the public hearing process were considered while finalizing the environmental assessment and mitigation measures for the project.

Is land being taken without the consent of the people?

No. The Land acquisition is being taken as per the LARR Act 2013 and other state-applicable laws of GoMP. The consents have been obtained as per the Act and accordingly the rehabilitation plan is being implemented. Under this project, a comprehensive R&R package has been announced by GoMP under which all R&R works are being undertaken. The rehabilitation plan is consent-based, and all affected families were given a choice between compensation under the normal land acquisition law or a more generous Special Package.

How will disputes regarding land ownership be handled?

Land ownership and entitlement issues are dealt with by competent revenue and land-acquisition authorities headed by the District Collector. Where there are disputes regarding title, succession, ownership or entitlement, the matter is processed in accordance with applicable law and established administrative/judicial procedures.

Compensation and the Special Rehabilitation Package

Whether any special package for R&R under KBLP has been announced by GoMP?

Yes, the GoMP announced a Special Package for the Resettlement and Rehabilitation of Project Affected Families (PAFs) in 2023. Under the Special Package, compensation for acquired land is paid at either the rate determined by the Act or ₹12.50 lakh per hectare, whichever is higher, with compensation for houses, trees, wells, tube wells and other immovable assets similarly determined under the Act. Eligible families are receiving a grant of ₹7 lakh for a plot in rural areas (₹6.50 lakh in urban areas), or lump-sum assistance of ₹12.50 lakh where a plot is not opted for; eligible Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe families in scheduled areas receive additional financial assistance under the approved package.

Who is considered a Project Affected Family (PAF) for getting R&R assistance under the LARR Act, 2013?

A Project Affected Family means a family whose land, house, property, forest rights, or main source of livelihood is affected due to land acquisition for the project.

Landowners whose land is acquired;

Persons whose livelihood is affected due to the acquisition;

Tenants, agricultural labourers and share-croppers whose livelihood is affected;

Scheduled Tribes and traditional forest dwellers whose recognised forest rights are affected; and

Other eligible families covered under Section 3(c) of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013.

Such families may be eligible for Rehabilitation & Resettlement (R&R) benefits as provided under the Act and applicable rules.

How is a family unit counted for R&R benefits in KBLP?

As per Section 3(m) of the LARR Act, 2013, a family includes the person, his/her spouse, minor children and dependent minor brothers and sisters.

For R&R benefits, the following are treated as separate family units:

Adult sons or daughters (18 years or above), whether married or unmarried.

Widows, divorcees and women deserted by their families are treated as separate families.

Thus, in KBLP, the number of PAFs is determined by identifying the eligible family units as per the LARR Act, 2013, based on the survey and verification of affected families.

What support is available under KBLP for families who do not own land but whose livelihood is affected by the project?

Under the LARR Act, 2013, land ownership is not the only basis for R&R benefits. Eligible landless families whose main source of livelihood is affected due to KBLP have also been considered as Project Affected Families (PAFs), subject to the eligibility conditions under the Act and applicable State Government provisions.

Such eligible families are provided R&R benefits as applicable under the approved R&R provisions of KBLP.

How are people assisted in earning their livelihood after relocation?

Under various schemes, they are provided dedicated livelihood restoration programs that provide vocational and skill-development training, financial grants for self-help groups, small business assistance, and priority employment in project operations.

What compensation do people get for their land?

Families are paid either the rate fixed under the land acquisition law, or ₹12.50 lakh per hectare as per the Special Package announced by GoMP, whichever amount is higher.

What about houses, trees and wells on the land?

Compensation for houses, trees, wells, tube wells and other fixed property is also given, calculated as per the law.

What if a family wants a new house plot instead of just cash?

Eligible families can get a grant of ₹7 lakh for a plot in rural areas, or ₹6.50 lakh in urban areas.

What if a family does not want a plot at all?

They can instead choose a one-time lump-sum payment of ₹12.50 lakh per family.

Is there extra help for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe families?

Yes. Eligible SC and ST families living in Scheduled Areas get additional financial assistance on top of the standard package.

Who approved this Special Package?

The Government of Madhya Pradesh approved it on 13 September 2023, following a decision of the State Cabinet on 9 September 2023.

How much compensation has been paid so far?

As of the latest figures, awards worth about ₹360.66 crore have been passed, of which about ₹321.97 crore (around 89%) has already been paid to families. In village-habitation areas alone, over 94% of the awarded amount has been distributed.

What about the total project-wide compensation figures?

Across the project, awards worth about ₹629.87 crore have been passed for 5,039 affected families, and about ₹604.745 crore (around 96%) has already been paid out. The remaining amount will be released once the required legal formalities are completed.

How is land compensation calculated and paid out?

Compensation is calculated transparently based on official market rates plus statutory resettlement allowances. Payments are transferred directly into verified bank accounts of landowners to prevent middlemen and unnecessary delays.

Are there special healthcare and educational initiatives?

Yes. Regular free medical checkup camps, mobile health vans, school infrastructure upgrades, and student scholarships are actively provided under ongoing community welfare programs.

What is KBLPA's approach towards affected families?

KBLPA recognizes that land acquisition affects not only land and property but also the lives and livelihoods of affected families. Accordingly, KBLPA is focusing on timely compensation, rehabilitation and resettlement, livelihood support, relocation wherever required, provision of basic civic amenities at resettlement sites, consultation with affected persons and grievance redressal. The objective is to ensure that Project Affected Families are treated with fairness, transparency and dignity throughout the rehabilitation and resettlement process.

Will affected landowners receive compensation?

Yes, Eligible landowners and other persons having recognized rights/interests in land are entitled to compensation and other admissible benefits in accordance with the applicable statutory framework.

The compensation process is intended to ensure that affected persons receive the benefits to which they are legally entitled.

Making Sure No One Is Left Out

What happens if someone's name was left out of the compensation list?

The district administration has re-surveyed affected villages in Chhatarpur and Panna at the request of displaced families, and people who were earlier left out have now been added to the compensation awards.

Who checks that the process stays fair and accurate?

The District Administration continuously reviews land records. In addition, a National Monitoring Committee, set up under the land acquisition law, oversees the entire rehabilitation process.

Who helps families with documentation and paperwork?

Dedicated Field Facilitation Officers visit villages weekly to assist families with entitlement verification, banking paperwork, and application submissions at zero cost.

Can affected families still raise complaints or grievances?

Yes. Grievances are regularly received and resolved. For example, the administration has held special camps to hear and settle complaints from displaced families in the affected villages.

What is KBLPA’s message to people affected by the project?

KBLPA’s message is clear: the development of Bundelkhand should go hand in hand with the rights, dignity and welfare of Project Affected Families. KBLPA is working with the concerned State Governments, district administrations and affected communities to implement land acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement (R&R), and environmental measures in accordance with applicable laws, approved plans and prescribed procedures. The objective is to ensure fairness, transparency and responsible implementation of the project.

Support for Displaced Families

Are the children of displaced families looked after?

Yes. Efforts are made to enrol their children in schools and Anganwadi centres so their education is not disrupted.

Is healthcare support provided to displaced families?

Yes. Health camps have been organised where people are medically examined, medicines are distributed, and drinking-water handpumps are repaired.

Do displaced families get access to other government welfare schemes?

Yes. Special camps are held so families can also benefit from other government schemes, such as those related to livestock, social security, and welfare schemes for women and girls.

Does the government stay in touch with displaced families after they relocate?

Yes, Regular contact is maintained with displaced families so that any difficulty is quickly identified and their grievances are resolved fairly and speedily.

Rights of Tribal and Forest-Dependent Communities

Are the rights of tribal communities protected in this project?

Yes. The rights of Scheduled Tribes and other forest-dependent communities are safeguarded under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, through a statutory process of recognising and settling forest rights.

Was the consent of local communities taken before forest clearance?

The concerned District Collectors initiated the process for obtaining the free, prior and informed consent of the relevant Gram Sabhas, as required under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006. It was on this basis, and subject to compliance with applicable statutory requirements, that Forest Clearance for the project was accorded by MoEF&CC on 03.10.2023.

Environmental and Legal Clearances

Has the project received all the required government clearances?

Yes. The project has received all the statutory clearances needed under law, including Environmental Clearance (2017), Wildlife Clearance (2016), Clearance from the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (2017), and Forest Clearance (2023).

Will KBLP have environmental impacts?

Like any major water-resources infrastructure project, KBLP has environmental impacts that require careful assessment and management.

The project has therefore incorporated environmental safeguards and an Environmental Management Plan (EMP), along with compliance with applicable environmental, forest and wildlife-related requirements.

The approach is based on the principle that development and environmental protection must progress together.

Whether the environmental impacts of KBLP were studied before implementation?

Yes. The environmental impacts of the Ken–Betwa Link Project (KBLP) were assessed through detailed environmental studies as part of the statutory clearance process. Based on these assessments, the project was granted Environmental Clearance on 25.08.2017, along with the required Wildlife Clearance and Forest Clearance, subject to prescribed conditions and mitigation measures.

The project is also implementing various environmental management, compensatory afforestation, wildlife conservation and biodiversity protection measures to address and minimize the identified environmental impacts.

How is the loss of forest area and biodiversity in the core area of Panna Tiger Reserve (PTR) being compensated under KBLP?

The environmental impacts of KBLP, including unavoidable forest loss and impacts on biodiversity, are being addressed through a combination of compensatory afforestation, wildlife conservation and habitat management, catchment area treatment and implementation of the Integrated Landscape Management Plan (ILMP) for the Greater Panna Landscape.

In addition, an equivalent area of non-forest land has been provided adjacent to the core area of Panna Tiger Reserve for compensatory purposes, which will contribute to strengthening the habitat and conservation landscape around the Reserve.

Funds have also been provided as per the conditions of the Forest and Wildlife Clearances for implementing approved conservation and mitigation measures. These measures aim to compensate for unavoidable forest loss, minimize ecological impacts and strengthen biodiversity and wildlife conservation in the wider landscape.

What is the concern regarding Panna Tiger Reserve?

The project has significant environmental and wildlife considerations because of its proximity and relationship with the Panna landscape. Accordingly, wildlife and forest-related safeguards have been incorporated into project planning and implementation.

The Government has also undertaken landscape-level planning and conservation measures in association with the project.

What are the measures being taken to protect the environment and the wildlife

The project is aimed at not only providing water security in the Bundelkhand but also ensuring the overall conservation of the region and especially for landscape-dependent species such as Tiger, Vulture and Gharial. Apart from taking mitigation measures as per the approved Environmental Management Plan, the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) has prepared a comprehensive Integrated Landscape Management Plan (ILMP) for the conservation of wildlife and biodiversity not only in Panna Tiger Reserve (PTR) but also in surrounding areas. The Integrated Landscape Management Plan in Greater Panna Landscape (GPL) is one of the major and unique conservation measures being initiated in the conservation history of India.

What is Greater Panna Landscape Council?

A comprehensive Integrated Landscape Management Plan (ILMP) has been prepared for the conservation of wildlife and biodiversity in Panna Tiger Reserve (PTR) & surrounding areas. To ensure systematic and time-bound implementation of the Greater Panna Landscape Management Plan, the Greater Panna Landscape Council (GPLC) has been constituted under the chairmanship of the Chief Secretary, Govt. of Madhya Pradesh, with members from all the stakeholders. Adequate financial provisions have been earmarked for the implementation of Environment Management Plan and Integrated Landscape Management Plan under the Ken-Betwa Link Project. This model will be a template for future development.

What is compensatory afforestation?

Where forest land is diverted for approved project purposes, compensatory afforestation and other prescribed measures are undertaken in accordance with applicable forest legislation and approvals. These measures are intended to compensate for permitted diversion of forest land and contribute to long-term ecological restoration.

Will KBLP affect biodiversity?

Environmental impacts on biodiversity have been considered as part of project planning. The project incorporates mitigation and conservation measures intended to reduce, manage and compensate for unavoidable impacts. Environmental monitoring will also be undertaken during construction and operation.

What is being done to make sure the project stays on track?

Compensation and rehabilitation work continues in a transparent, fair and time-bound manner, with local officials in ongoing contact with affected families to resolve issues quickly.

What is the larger goal of the project going forward?

The goal is to balance the region's development needs with the rights and welfare of affected families — completing rehabilitation with dignity while delivering long-term irrigation, drinking water and power benefits to Bundelkhand.

Where can people get more information about the project?

More information is available on the official KBLPA website: www.kblpa.gov.in, the Ministry of Jal Shakti and the District Administrations of Chhatarpur and Panna.

headline: Union Health Minister Shri JP Nadda Reviews H1N1 Influenza Preparedness; Emphasises Vigilance and Robust Surveillance

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Shri JP Nadda Reviews H1N1 Influenza Preparedness; Emphasises Vigilance and Robust Surveillance

21 AUG 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Shri JP Nadda, today reviewed the prevailing situation and preparedness for H1N1 Influenza in the country, with particular focus on the National Capital. Delhi Health Minister Dr. Pankaj Kumar Singh also attended the meeting.

The Union Health Minister reviewed the national surveillance and epidemiological situation, Influenza-like illness (ILI) and Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) trends, testing and laboratory surveillance, and preparedness of healthcare facilities to manage seasonal influenza cases. Shri Nadda emphasised the need for continued vigilance, robust surveillance and proactive preparedness, with close monitoring of influenza trends and timely identification and management of any unusual increase or clustering of cases.

The preparedness of healthcare facilities in Delhi was reviewed, including the availability of hospital beds, critical care facilities, oxygen-supported beds, ventilators, essential medicines, diagnostics, and other critical supplies. The Minister stressed the importance of adequate surge capacity and seamless referral mechanisms, particularly for patients requiring specialised or critical care.

The Union Health Minister called for continued strengthening of early detection, timely testing and appropriate clinical management of influenza cases, along with effective utilisation of the existing surveillance and laboratory network.

Earlier, on 10th July 2026, the Union Health Secretary had written to all States/UTs advising them to strengthen preparedness and surveillance for Acute Respiratory Illness (ARI) and ensure healthcare facilities remain adequately prepared.

Shri Nadda also emphasised public awareness and preventive health practices, including respiratory hygiene and hand hygiene, and advised individuals with persistent or severe respiratory symptoms, breathing difficulty or other warning signs to seek medical advice promptly.

The Union Health Minister reiterated that the situation is being closely and continuously monitored, while emphasising the need for sustained and coordinated efforts for the prevention and control of seasonal diseases, including Dengue and Malaria. Shri Nadda called for a proactive and preparedness-oriented approach by State Governments, with active participation of Municipal Councillors and other local bodies in generating awareness among communities on the prevention, spread and control of seasonal diseases.

Highlighting the increase in TB detection in the National Capital through the active involvement of local bodies and a whole-of-government approach, the Union Minister stressed the importance of active participation of public representatives at all levels in disseminating factual and evidence-based information and strengthening community engagement.

The Ministry continues to coordinate closely with States/UTs, hospitals, laboratories and other stakeholders to ensure effective surveillance, early detection, timely clinical management and proactive preparedness for seasonal influenza, including H1N1.

The meeting was also attended by Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava; Additional Secretary (Public Health) Dr. Rakesh Gupta; Delhi State Health Secretary Shri Rupesh Kumar Thakur and other senior officers.
